title: Baptism
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Baptism is the public identification of a believer with Jesus Christ and His people. It points to union with Christ in His death, burial, and resurrection and marks entrance into visible discipleship.
summary: Baptism is the public identification of a believer with Jesus Christ and His people. It points to union with Christ in His death, burial, and resurrection and marks entrance into visible discipleship.
christFocus: Jesus Christ commands baptism and gives it meaning through His saving work. Baptism points to His death, resurrection, cleansing, lordship, and the believer’s belonging to Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Baptism is commanded by Christ as part of disciple-making. Those who respond to the Gospel are to be baptized in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

Baptism does not save by the outward act itself. Salvation is by grace through faith in Christ. Yet baptism is a serious public sign of identification with Christ and His people.

Scripture connects baptism with the believer’s union with Christ in death and resurrection. It visibly proclaims that the old life is judged in Christ and new life has begun.

Baptism also identifies believers with the visible people of God. It is not merely private spirituality, but public discipleship under the lordship of Jesus.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some treat baptism as unnecessary, while others trust the act apart from living faith. Scripture avoids both errors by presenting baptism as commanded, meaningful, and connected to discipleship.

This doctrine matters because Christ’s people should not be ashamed to identify with Him. Baptism publicly says that the believer belongs to Jesus and is called to walk in newness of life.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive baptism as Christ commanded, not as empty ritual or human performance. If you have been baptized, remember what it signifies: you belong to Christ, have been joined to His people, and are called to walk in new life. Teach baptism as part of faithful discipleship.
